blocks.tex:
The concise existence statement records the polygon and its radii. Curvature
and local nonconcyclicity follow for that same polygon, independently of any
other witness chosen by an existence theorem. The fuller original theorem
and its proof remain in the preceding supporting chapters.

blocks.label: presentation:geometric-converse
blocks.title: A polygon with the prescribed consecutive radii
blocks.body:
For $n\ge4$, a positive cyclic radius word with two distinct plateau maxima
and two distinct plateau minima admits a coherent convex polygon $v$ with
$R_i(v)=r_i$ for every $i$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.tabachnikov_converse_geometric
lean.code:
theorem tabachnikov_converse_geometric [NeZero n] (hn : 4 ≤ n) {r : ZMod n → ℝ}
    (hr : ∀ i, 0 < r i) (hext : IsPlateauTwoMaxTwoMin r) :
    ∃ v : ZMod n → ℂ, IsCoherentConvexPolygon v ∧
      ∀ i, vertexCircumradius v i = r i :=
  (tabachnikov_converse hn hr hext).imp fun _ h ↦ ⟨h.1, h.2.1⟩

blocks.tex:
The full radius converse supplies one such polygon, together with further
curvature and nonconcyclicity conclusions. Retain its coherence and exact
radius equations. No hypothesis or geometric part of the realization changes.

blocks.label: presentation:curvature
blocks.title: Signed curvature of the same polygon
blocks.body:
If $v$ is a coherent convex polygon and $R_i(v)=r_i$ for all $i$, then
its signed Menger curvature at every vertex is $\kappa_i(v)=1/r_i$.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsCoherentConvexPolygon.signedMengerR2_eq_inv_of_radii
lean.code:
lemma IsCoherentConvexPolygon.signedMengerR2_eq_inv_of_radii
    {v : ZMod n → ℂ} {r : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : IsCoherentConvexPolygon v)
    (hrad : ∀ i, vertexCircumradius v i = r i) (i : ZMod n) :
    signedMengerR2 (v (i - 1)) (v i) (v (i + 1)) = 1 / r i := by
  simpa only [one_div_one_div, SignedMengerProfile_apply] using
    congrArg (fun x : ℝ ↦ 1 / x) ((h.vertexCircumradius_eq_inv i).symm.trans (hrad i))

deps.title: Moderate arcs give coherence and exact Menger curvature
deps.label: detail:discrete-coherence

deps.title: Circumradius is reciprocal absolute Menger curvature
deps.label: detail:discrete-circumradius

blocks.tex:
Strict positive orientation makes the signed curvature positive.
The circumradius identity is $R_i(v)=1/\kappa_i(v)$. Substitute the
prescribed radius and take reciprocals, using $1/(1/x)=x$.

blocks.label: presentation:four-points
blocks.title: Unequal adjacent radii exclude four concyclic vertices
blocks.body:
For the same polygon, if $r_i\ne r_{i+1}$, the four consecutive vertices
$v_{i-1},v_i,v_{i+1},v_{i+2}$ are not concyclic. No inequality is needed
at any other pair of adjacent radii.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.IsCoherentConvexPolygon.not_concyclic4_of_radius_ne
lean.code:
lemma IsCoherentConvexPolygon.not_concyclic4_of_radius_ne
    {v : ZMod n → ℂ} {r : ZMod n → ℝ} (h : IsCoherentConvexPolygon v)
    (hrad : ∀ i, vertexCircumradius v i = r i) (i : ZMod n)
    (hne : r i ≠ r (i + 1)) :
    ¬ Concyclic4 (v (i - 1)) (v i) (v (i + 1)) (v (i + 2)) :=
  fun hcon ↦ hne ((hrad i).symm.trans
    ((vertexCircumradius_eq_of_concyclic i (h.2.2 i).1 (h.2.2 (i + 1)).1 hcon).trans
      (hrad (i + 1))))

deps.title: Moderate arcs give coherence and exact Menger curvature
deps.label: detail:discrete-coherence

deps.title: Circumradius is reciprocal absolute Menger curvature
deps.label: detail:discrete-circumradius

blocks.tex:
Each overlapping triple is noncollinear. If all four vertices belonged to
one circle, uniqueness of each triple's circumcircle would make their
circumradii equal. Substituting $R_i(v)=r_i$ and $R_{i+1}(v)=r_{i+1}$
contradicts the assumed inequality.

blocks.label: presentation:local
blocks.title: Local choice from a strict four-vertex window
blocks.body:
A positive cyclic profile with a strict four-vertex window at some level
has a local $C^1$ coherent realization family. Neither an explicit lower
bound on $n$ nor a separate nonconstancy assumption is needed: the four
strictly ordered indices and alternating inequalities already imply them.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.localContinuousRealization_of_dfv
lean.code:
theorem localContinuousRealization_of_dfv
    {κ₀ : ZMod n → ℝ} {c : ℝ} (hκ₀ : ∀ i, 0 < κ₀ i) (hdfv : DFV κ₀ c) :
    Nonempty (LocalDiscreteRealizationFamily κ₀) := by
  obtain ⟨A⟩ := nonempty_regularFourAnchor_of_dfv hκ₀ hdfv
  exact A.nonempty_localDiscreteRealizationFamily hκ₀

deps.title: Local coherent choice at every nonconstant admissible profile
deps.label: thm:tabachnikov_local_continuity

blocks.tex:
The window produces a regular four-active-edge anchor. The local opening
theorem at that anchor gives an open neighborhood and a $C^1$ choice of
lengths. The developed vertices, exact curvature, moderate arcs, closure,
full turn, and simplicity all belong to the same family.

blocks.label: presentation:hexagon
blocks.title: The hexagon obstruction without an orientation premise
blocks.body:
There is no continuous vertex path on $[0,1]$ whose members are simple
Dahlberg-regular hexagons with the prescribed signed Menger band profile
$\kappa_s$. A separate positive-orientation hypothesis is unnecessary.

lean.name: Gluck.Discrete.GlobalContinuity.no_continuous_regular_hexagon_path
lean.code:
theorem no_continuous_regular_hexagon_path :
    ¬ ∃ p : ℝ → (ZMod 6 → ℂ), ContinuousOn p (Set.Icc 0 1) ∧
      ∀ s ∈ Set.Icc (0 : ℝ) 1,
        IsSimplePolygon (p s) ∧ DahlbergRegular (p s) ∧
        SignedMengerProfile (p s) = bandProfile s :=
  fun ⟨p, hp, h⟩ ↦ no_continuous_coherent_hexagon_path
    ⟨p, hp, fun s hs ↦ ⟨(h s hs).1, (h s hs).2.1,
      positivePolygonOrientation_iff_signedMengerProfile_pos.mpr
        (by simpa only [(h s hs).2.2] using bandProfile_pos hs), (h s hs).2.2⟩⟩

deps.title: No continuous choice of the actual polygons
deps.label: detail:hexagon-geometric-obstruction

blocks.tex:
Every value of the band profile is positive. In the signed Menger formula,
positivity forces the oriented determinant of each consecutive triple to be
positive. Thus every purported member satisfies the orientation hypothesis
of the previously proved geometric hexagon obstruction, a contradiction.
